evidence.s1_requirements: All step 1 requirements are met. `snapshot()`/`restore()` are on BehaviourTree (src/BehaviourTree.ts:149-185). `BehaviourTreeSnapshot` and `NodeSnapshot` are exported as types (src/index.ts). The snapshot holds plain state strings, child arrays and numeric progress, and a test checks the JSON round trip (test/Snapshot.spec.ts:41-55). Repeat and retry counts are saved, including the random target (Repeat.ts:127-159, Retry.ts). The lotto's picked child is saved as `selectedChildIndex` (Lotto.ts:73-109). Wait saves `totalDuration` and `waitedDuration`. On restore, `initialUpdateTime = now - waitedDuration` (Wait.ts:150-156), so time between snapshot and restore is not counted in clock mode; with getDeltaTime the accumulated time is restored. A finished tree restores as finished, and step() resets and re-randomises (test at Snapshot.spec.ts:949-998). The README has the API entries and an example.
evidence.s1_correctness: Each node saves progress only when it is not READY (Node.ts:350-352), and READY nodes re-initialise in onUpdate, so stale internal fields are harmless. Lotto handles being resolved by a guard before it picked a child (getProgress returns {} and restore accepts a missing index unless RUNNING; Lotto.ts:96-100, tested at 1207-1219). Clock-mode wait counts the time since the last step at snapshot time (Wait.ts:121-123). Restoring clears any pending promise in Action, so a target tree's in-flight promise cannot leak in (Action.ts:195-201). A 51-step lockstep test covers race, repeat, selector, flip, retry, all, lotto, succeed, parallel, branch, fail, a while guard, entry/exit callbacks and random counts and durations, comparing node details, snapshots, agent call logs and random-call counts (Snapshot.spec.ts:242-353). I traced Sequence, Parallel, Race, All, Repeat and Retry against children restored as READY or RUNNING and found no defect.
evidence.s2_validation: `getDefinitionIdentifier` canonicalises the validated JSON (sorted keys, dropped undefined, default `args: []` and `succeedOnAbort: false`, root nodes sorted by id) and then hashes it (BehaviourTreeDefinitionUtilities.ts:2082-2139 in all.patch). A test shows a complex MDSL definition and its reordered JSON equivalent get the same identifier (Snapshot.spec.ts:95-125), and an MDSL↔JSON restore round trip passes (208-240). A mismatch throws "error restoring tree: the snapshot does not match the tree's definition" (BehaviourTree.ts:2048-2050 in all.patch). Tests cover different structure, args, callback and guard (518-562). null, undefined, string, number, boolean, array, {} and partial objects are rejected, and the tree is checked unchanged afterwards (486-516). Restore validates everything in prepareRestore before applying anything, so it is atomic. A pending-promise action is saved as READY (Action.ts:179-189) and is re-called on the next step, with its entry callback (tests at 758-906). This is documented under README 'Limitations' and in the snapshot() API entry.
evidence.s3_fixes: Report 1 is fixed at its cause: Node.prepareRestore now sets `this._state` directly instead of calling `setState` (step3.patch Node.ts:147-149). The agent's own step 1 test, which asserted the opposite, was rewritten, and a test that the next step still reports changes was added (Snapshot.spec.ts:693-747). Report 2 needed no code change, since snapshots are built fresh and restore copies only primitives. The agent added a test-only commit (9d9ca2f) that checks independence and equality right after restore, in both time modes. However, the README marks an exception: in clock mode a snapshot taken right after restore is not equal if any milliseconds pass ('apart from the time spent by any wait node that is measuring time with the clock'). The report as written asks for equality, so this is documented rather than resolved. There are no unrelated changes in step 3.
evidence.design: Each node owns its own state through overridable `getProgress`/`prepareProgressRestore` hooks (Node.ts:361-375). The two-phase validate-then-apply closure design gives an atomic restore. The public surface is small: two methods and two exported types. Weaknesses: `NodeSnapshot` is one flat type with optional fields for every node kind rather than a per-node type (Node.ts:2186-2231 in all.patch). A new `isNonNegativeInteger` was added in Utilities.ts although `isInteger` already exists in BehaviourTreeDefinitionUtilities, and Wait adds a local `isDuration`. The try/catch in `snapshot()` became dead code once step 2 stopped getSnapshot from throwing (BehaviourTree.ts:2026-2030). `getChildren` was converted from arrow properties to methods in Composite and Decorator, which is needed for the base override and was done in its own refactor commit.
evidence.tests: test/Snapshot.spec.ts (1280 lines) uses mocha, chai and sinon fake timers like the existing suites. It covers the JSON round trip, the lockstep test across every node type at every step, the finished-tree rerun with new random choices, repeat and retry with fixed and random counts (random throws in the restored tree to prove it is not called again), lotto, wait in clock mode, getDeltaTime mode, clock set back and varying deltas, guard-resolved lotto, the definition-identifier stability pin and equivalences, every invalid input with an unchanged tree, field-level validation, onNodeStateChange, pending, settled-unhandled and stale promises, and both step 3 reports in both time modes. The only existing suite touched is test/nodes/leaf/Action.spec.ts, which gained one test (all.patch:4022-4047); nothing was removed or weakened.
evidence.docs: The README adds a feature bullet, snapshot()/restore() API entries, and a 'Saving and Restoring Trees' section. It has a correct workflow example (`import { State, BehaviourTree } from "mistreevous"`, restore from a file, step, save), a sample snapshot whose identifier a test pins, and notes on what is saved, wait timing, restore rules and a Limitations section for pending promises next to the API. The onNodeStateChange option row was updated in step 3. Version History follows the table convention: 4.4.0 for the feature, edited in step 2 because it was not yet released, then 4.4.1 for the step 3 fix. package.json and package-lock.json were bumped to match.
evidence.process: 23 commits with conventional prefixes (feat/test/fix/docs/refactor/build), each focused, with dist regeneration kept in separate build commits. Messages describe the changes. Commit 12b0d55 bundles two concerns: refusing to snapshot promise actions, and the identity-based fix that ignores stale promises. That fix is a pre-existing baseline bug (a reset action's old promise could be applied to the next run); it was needed for restore correctness and is documented in Version History and covered by a test in Action.spec.ts. No new dependencies and no unrequested features.

unmet_requirements: Step 3 report 2 (partly met): a snapshot taken right after restore equals the original only if no clock time passes; the README documents an exception for clock-mode wait nodes instead of guaranteeing equality.
strengths: The two-phase validate-then-apply restore makes rejected restores atomic, and each node type owns its saved progress through small overridable hooks.

A very strong test suite: a lockstep test over every node type at every step compares node details, snapshots, agent calls and random-call counts, plus focused tests for wait in both time modes, lotto guard edge cases, pending promises and every invalid input.
MDSL and JSON equivalence is handled by canonicalising the validated definition before hashing, and the README documents the API, format, timing rules and pending-promise limitation accurately.
issues: Report 2 is only partly met: in clock mode a snapshot taken right after restore differs if any milliseconds pass, and the README documents this exception rather than making the snapshot equal.

Small design smells: `NodeSnapshot` is one flat type with optional fields for every node kind, `isNonNegativeInteger`/`isDuration` duplicate the existing `isInteger` helper, and the try/catch in `snapshot()` is dead code after step 2.
Commit 12b0d55 bundles a feature with a fix to a pre-existing baseline bug (stale promise after reset); the fix is justified and documented but would read better as its own commit.
review.verdict: The snapshot/restore feature is correct across all node types and edge cases, with atomic validated restores, definition matching that treats MDSL and equivalent JSON as the same definition, and an unusually thorough, well-structured test suite and README. The remaining points are minor: a documented clock-mode exception to snapshot equality, a few duplicated helpers and dead code, and one bundled commit. I would merge it.
